questions.question_text: My father has pancreatic cancer and is considering volunteering for research studies. What opportunities exist?

rubric_items.description: The response should state that standard of care treatment for pancreatic cancer can include surgery and/or chemotherapy, depending on how advanced the disease is, as outlined in the NCCN guidelines version 2.2025
The response should state that patients with pancreatic cancer should undergo genetic testing for mutations that have been inherited, which may provide targeted therapy options

The response should state that patients with pancreatic cancer should have molecular evaluation of their tumor tissue to understand if there are particular abnormalities in their cancer that might provide targeted therapy options
The response should include the definitions of different types of research studies including randomized clinical trials and observational studies

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and we're trying to understand treatment resistance. Why do treatments stop working?

rubric_items.description: The response must explicitly explain how normal cells acquire mutations that transform them into malignant cells. Synonyms for "mutations" include "genetic changes" or "alterations."
The response must explicitly describe how malignant cells evade the body's immune system. Synonyms for "evade" include "avoid" or "escape."
The response must explicitly describe the mechanisms of action for chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and radiation in killing cancer cells. Synonyms for "mechanisms of action" include "ways" or "methods."

The response must thoroughly cover multiple mechanisms of treatment resistance, including genetic mutations, tumor heterogeneity, drug efflux, alterations in drug targets, epigenetic changes, adaptive responses, and the tumor microenvironment. Synonyms for "mechanisms" include "methods" or "ways."

The response must explicitly mention cancer stem cells and connect them to specific resistance mechanisms such as drug efflux pumps, enhanced DNA repair, or immune evasion. Synonyms for "connect" include "link" or "associate."
The response must explicitly state that surviving resistant cells can repopulate the tumor after most cells are killed by treatment. Synonyms for "repopulate" include "regrow" or "rebuild."

The response must explicitly describe that with every treatment, a selective pressure is applied to cancer cells. Synonyms for "selective pressure" include "evolutionary pressure" or "adaptive pressure."

The response must mention that cancer treatments may need to be dose-reduced if the patient has unacceptable toxicity, which may reduce the efficacy of the treatment. Synonyms for "dose-reduced" include "lowered" or "decreased."
The response must state that this topic is being widely researched and cite at least one source from the literature. Synonyms for "cite" include "reference" or "mention."

questions.question_text: My husband has pancreatic cancer and we want to understand more about tumor suppressor genes. How do these relate to cancer development?

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and we're considering professional counseling. What type of counselor should we look for?

rubric_items.description: The response must list at least three types of mental health care providers, including their credentials and any limitations in practice.

questions.question_text: My father has pancreatic cancer and his doctors mentioned DNA damage response pathways. How do these relate to treatment options?

questions.question_text: My mother has pancreatic cancer and we're trying to understand the role of inflammation in cancer progression. How is this managed?

rubric_items.description: The response must clearly define inflammation using terms such as "immune response," "tissue injury," or "protective mechanism."

The response must describe at least two medical strategies for managing inflammation, such as "targeted therapies," "immunotherapies," "steroids," or "pain management."
The response must state that there is no formal, evidence-based strategy to quantify and target inflammation in cancer patients.
The response must state that treating the cancer itself, such as through "surgery" or "radiation," is postulated to improve cancer-related inflammation.
The response must mention chronic pancreatitis or chronic pancreatic injury as a factor in cancer formation and provide at least one scientific reference with a PMID.
The response must recommend at least two lifestyle interventions to decrease inflammation, such as "plant-based diet," "exercise," "hydration," or "good quality sleep."
The response must recommend against nicotine and alcohol use and reference their role in promoting inflammation.
The response must recommend that the patient report any symptoms to their oncology team for symptom management.

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and we're dealing with medication management challenges. What systems can help organize this?

questions.question_text: My husband has pancreatic cancer and we want to understand more about oncogenes. How do these contribute to cancer development?

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and we're trying to understand treatment sequencing. Does the order of treatments matter?

questions.question_text: My mother has pancreatic cancer and we're dealing with communication challenges with the medical team. How can we improve this?

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and we want to understand more about circadian rhythms in cancer. How do these affect treatment timing?

questions.question_text: My loved one has pancreatic cancer and we're dealing with insurance coverage for experimental treatments. What options do we have?

rubric_items.description: The response must explicitly recommend that the patient and/or family discuss insurance coverage issues with the oncology team administering the experimental treatment. Synonyms for "discuss" include "consult," "talk to," or "communicate with."

The response must mention that financial assistance programs are available for some experimental drugs and explicitly state that this varies from drug to drug, requiring inquiry. Synonyms for "inquire" include "ask about," "investigate," or "research."

The response must state that many clinical trial drugs are free of cost to patients and explicitly mention that travel to and from the trial center is often not covered. Synonyms for "mention" include "note," "state," or "indicate."
The response must describe what "compassionate use" is and recommend that the patient/family ask their oncology team about this. Synonyms for "describe" include "explain," "define," or "clarify."

The response must recommend that the patient discuss their concerns with their cancer center's financial team and/or patient advocacy office. Synonyms for "recommend" include "suggest," "advise," or "propose."

The response must recommend that the patient seek out patient advocacy groups online to learn how other patients navigated the same issues. Synonyms for "seek out" include "look for," "search for," or "find."
